description: Tiny hand-built rule/case integration witnesses using actual crate APIs.
forward: Construct deterministic Clauses/Rules/Jurisdictions/Facts without parser models. Existing tests cover empty match, path count changes, broad reading, conflict resolution, report determinism, flag filtering, stats, devices and absurd criteria. Wave31 adds explicit count enumeration, tie/zero-tip boundaries, postprocessing/metrics, codec/status fibers and lookup order.
inverse: The selected test traces cannot query teacher, parse a corpus or write production rules because fixtures call in-memory helpers/report only. A passing test does not exclude bugs outside asserted observations.

A named pass constrains implementation only at executed fixture/assertion points; all implementations agreeing there are compatible. Test result alone cannot reconstruct the fixture values or certify whole APIs.

wave31 enumerates every mixed-radix assignment and calls evaluate, aggregates verdicts, compares count() output and total. It tests count/evaluate correspondence, not independent correctness of evaluate semantics.
Existing shuffled-rule and removed-condition comparisons alter fixture inputs, not compiled production source. They demonstrate sensitivity but are counted separately from compiled source mutants.
Exact selected names run twice debug and twice release, sorted named outcomes compared. Report determinism is also asserted in-process; elapsed timings are excluded and no throughput gain inferred.

Mutating count weight or precedence tie in actual court source and modal tie in report should compile but fail chosen assertion. Restore exact bytes/hash then rerun; compile failure alone is not a successful negative control.
limitations: Partial source-derived models and finite correspondence only
